title: Checkout failing with 5xx during lunch peak (HikariCP pool exhausted)
impact: 11.4% of checkout requests failed for 94 minutes during lunch peak; about 6,800 orders abandoned (estimated Rs 31 lakh GMV).
logs:
2026-04-18T11:03:52.118+05:30 WARN  [http-nio-8080-exec-87] c.z.h.p.HikariPool : HikariPool-1 - Connection is not available, request timed out after 30000ms (total=40, active=40, idle=0, waiting=212)
2026-04-18T11:03:52.121+05:30 ERROR [http-nio-8080-exec-87] o.h.e.j.s.SqlExceptionHelper : HikariPool-1 - Connection is not available, request timed out after 30000ms.
2026-04-18T11:03:52.140+05:30 ERROR [http-nio-8080-exec-87] c.b.checkout.api.OrderController : POST /v2/checkout failed traceId=7f3a9c2e1b44 status=503 cause=CannotCreateTransactionException

timeline.event: orders-db rejects connections: FATAL sorry, too many clients already; payments-gateway and rider-dispatch also fail
Arjun Mehta finds 38 'idle in transaction' sessions from application_name=inventory-reconcile holding row locks on stock_levels
inventory-reconcile CronJob suspended; idle-in-transaction sessions terminated

root_cause: inventory-sync v3.8.0 changed the inventory-reconcile CronJob schedule to '30 5 * * *' assuming IST, but Kubernetes CronJobs run in UTC, so the job ran at 11:00 IST (lunch peak). The job opens one transaction per warehouse, locks stock_levels rows with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE and then calls the slow WMS API (~40s per warehouse), leaving sessions 'idle in transaction'. checkout-api's stock reservation UPDATE blocks on those locks, every HikariCP connection ends up waiting, and the pool is exhausted.
contributing_factors: No idle_in_transaction_session_timeout on the reconcile role
No alert on idle-in-transaction session count
CronJob spec had no timeZone field

remediations.action: Rolling restart of checkout-api
remediations.result: Errors dropped for about 4 minutes, then the pool was exhausted again because the blocking row locks were still held by inventory-reconcile.

remediations.action: Scaled checkout-api HPA minReplicas from 12 to 20
remediations.result: 20 pods x 40 connections exceeded orders-db max_connections=500; orders-db returned 'FATAL: sorry, too many clients already' and payments-gateway and rider-dispatch lost database access for 4 minutes.

remediations.action: Suspended the inventory-reconcile CronJob and terminated idle-in-transaction sessions older than 60 seconds
remediations.command: kubectl patch cronjob inventory-reconcile -n inventory -p '{"spec":{"suspend":true}}' && psql -h orders-db -c "SELECT pg_terminate_backend(pid) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE state = 'idle in transaction' AND application_name = 'inventory-reconcile' AND now() - state_change > interval '60 seconds';"
remediations.result: Row locks released and the HikariCP pool recovered within 3 minutes.

action_items.item: Set idle_in_transaction_session_timeout = '60s' for the inventory_reconcile database role
Add timeZone: Asia/Kolkata to CronJob specs and move reconcile back to 03:00 IST
Alert when pg_stat_activity shows more than 10 idle-in-transaction sessions

title: Partner API TLS certificate expired on partners.basketbolt.in
detected_by: Brand partner (FMCG distributor) email: inventory push API failing
impact: Partner inventory pushes failed for 68 minutes; 14 brand partners affected, no customer-facing impact.
symptoms: x509: certificate has expired or is not yet valid
cert-manager Certificate partners-basketbolt-in not Ready for 30 days
logs:
2026-04-29T09:10:44+05:30 partner-ingest: Post "https://partners.basketbolt.in/v1/inventory": x509: certificate has expired or is not yet valid: current time 2026-04-29T03:40:44Z is after 2026-04-29T00:00:00Z
cert-manager E0429 03:41:02 controller.go:167] "re-queuing item due to error processing" err="failed to change Route 53 record set: AccessDenied: User: arn:aws:sts::482193550871:assumed-role/cert-manager-irsa/cert-manager is not authorized to perform: route53:ChangeResourceRecordSets on resource: arn:aws:route53:::hostedzone/Z07412963KXQ8T2M1VQ4"

timeline.event: Found Route 53 AccessDenied in cert-manager logs, traced to infra PR #1187
Reverted IAM policy with terraform apply

root_cause: The Terraform IAM refactor in infra PR #1187 removed route53:ChangeResourceRecordSets from the cert-manager IRSA role. DNS-01 renewals failed silently for 30 days until the certificate expired. There was no alert on certificate expiry.
contributing_factors: No certificate expiry alert
IAM change was not tested against cert-manager

remediations.action: Restarted cert-manager pods
remediations.result: No effect; the failure was an IAM permission problem, not a stuck controller.

remediations.action: Restored the Route 53 permission for the cert-manager IRSA role and forced certificate renewal
remediations.command: terraform apply -target=aws_iam_role_policy.cert_manager && cmctl renew partners-basketbolt-in -n edge
remediations.result: New certificate issued 4 minutes after renewal.

action_items.item: Prometheus alert when certmanager_certificate_expiration_timestamp_seconds - time() < 14 days
Policy test for cert-manager IAM role in CI

title: UPI payment success rate dropped to 71% (NovaPay collect timeouts)

2026-05-09T19:41:07.553+05:30 level=error msg="payment failed" reason=PSP_TIMEOUT psp=novapay order_id=ORD-88120451 attempt=1

Join NovaPay status webhook into #psp-novapay-bridge

title: Intermittent 5xx across services: DNS lookup timeouts (CoreDNS saturated)
impact: 1-4% intermittent 5xx on checkout-api, search-api and notification-svc for 69 minutes during a marketing campaign (3x traffic).
symptoms: CoreDNS pods CPU throttled at 200m limit
logs:
2026-05-21T14:21:58.311+05:30 checkout-api: dial tcp: lookup orders-db.internal.basketbolt.in on 172.20.0.10:53: read udp 10.4.12.9:51544->172.20.0.10:53: i/o timeout
2026-05-21T14:22:03.902+05:30 coredns-7d8f9c6b5-k2x9q [ERROR] plugin/errors: 2 api.upixpress.in.checkout.svc.cluster.local. A: read udp 10.4.3.21:40211->10.0.0.2:53: i/o timeout

timeline.event: Restarted checkout-api and search-api pods, no improvement
CoreDNS found CPU-throttled; ndots:5 causing 5 lookups per external hostname
CoreDNS scaled 2 -> 6 replicas and CPU limit raised to 1 core

root_cause: Campaign traffic tripled DNS query volume. With the default ndots:5 each external hostname produced up to five search-domain lookups, and only two CoreDNS replicas with a 200m CPU limit served the cluster, so CoreDNS was throttled and queries timed out.
contributing_factors: No NodeLocal DNSCache
Default ndots:5 on high-QPS services

remediations.action: Restarted affected application pods
remediations.result: No improvement; the bottleneck was CoreDNS, not the applications.

remediations.action: Scaled CoreDNS from 2 to 6 replicas and raised its CPU limit
remediations.result: DNS timeouts stopped within 8 minutes.

action_items.item: Deploy NodeLocal DNSCache DaemonSet (node-local-dns)
Set dnsConfig ndots:2 on high-QPS services

title: Out-of-stock items shown as available: Kafka consumer lag 1.2M on inventory.updates
detected_by: Kafka consumer lag alert (> 200k) and rising order-cancellation rate
impact: 12% of catalog showed stale stock for 107 minutes; order cancellations due to out-of-stock rose to 8%.
symptoms: Same offset retried thousands of times
logs: 2026-06-02T08:14:41.006+05:30 inventory-sync-consumer-5 ERROR Failed to process record topic=inventory.updates partition=3 offset=88412190: ValidationError: sku_id 'KND02-000000' does not match pattern ^[A-Z]{3}\d{2}-\d{6}$ (retry 1874)

timeline.event: Poison record identified: malformed SKU from new warehouse HYD-KONDAPUR-02 WMS integration
Offset moved to DLQ with kafka-dlq-skip; validator patched

root_cause: The new warehouse HYD-KONDAPUR-02 went live with a WMS integration that emitted malformed SKU ids for bundled items. The consumer retried the poison record forever (no dead-letter queue), blocking partition 3 of inventory.updates.
contributing_factors: No automatic DLQ after N retries
No schema contract test for new warehouse integrations

remediations.action: Scaled inventory-sync consumers from 6 to 12
remediations.result: No effect: the topic has 6 partitions so the extra consumers sat idle, and the blocked partition stayed blocked.

remediations.action: Moved the poison offset to the dead-letter queue and patched the SKU validator
remediations.result: Partition 3 resumed; 1.2M lag drained in 22 minutes.

action_items.item: Automatic DLQ after 3 retries in inventory-sync (v3.11.0)
SKU schema contract test in the warehouse onboarding checklist

title: Rider assignment stalled: Redis OOM on dispatch-cache during cricket final
impact: Rider assignment stalled for 53 minutes during the cricket final demand spike; 2,900 orders delayed beyond the 10-minute promise.
logs:
2026-06-21T21:47:55.431+05:30 rider-dispatch level=error msg="assign_rider failed" order_id=ORD-90233871 err="OOM command not allowed when used memory > 'maxmemory'."
2026-06-21T21:48:02.117+05:30 dispatch-cache INFO memory: used_memory_human:12.90G maxmemory_human:13.00G maxmemory_policy:noeviction

timeline.event: FLUSHALL proposed; rejected by incident commander because it would wipe live assignments
Active assignment keys evicted: 180 riders received duplicate orders; policy reverted
Found 4.1M rider:loc keys without TTL since v2.4.0

root_cause: rider-dispatch v2.4.0 moved rider location writes to a GEOADD pipeline and dropped the EXPIRE on rider:loc:{rider_id} keys. Stale locations accumulated for 12 days until the cricket final demand spike filled the remaining memory.
contributing_factors: No alert on dispatch-cache memory > 80%
No TTL assertion in tests

remediations.action: Switched dispatch-cache maxmemory-policy to allkeys-lru
remediations.command: redis-cli -h dispatch-cache CONFIG SET maxmemory-policy allkeys-lru
remediations.result: Redis evicted active assignment keys; 180 riders received duplicate orders. Reverted after 4 minutes.

remediations.action: Purged stale rider location keys and shipped hotfix v2.4.1 restoring the 15-minute TTL
remediations.result: Freed 7.8GB; assignment latency normal within 6 minutes.

action_items.item: Alert when dispatch-cache used_memory > 80% of maxmemory
Unit test asserting TTL on rider:loc keys

title: Search latency p99 9s: OpenSearch parent circuit breaker tripping
impact: Search p99 latency 9s and 6% failed searches for 67 minutes during lunch; search-to-cart conversion down 18%.
logs: 2026-06-28T13:04:51.822+05:30 search-api ERROR OpenSearchStatusException[OpenSearch exception [type=circuit_breaking_exception, reason=[parent] Data too large, data for [<http_request>] would be [7.8gb/7.8gb], which is larger than the limit of [7.6gb/7.6gb], real usage: [7.8gb/7.8gb]]]

timeline.event: Rolling restart of OpenSearch data nodes started
Shard relocation storm; cluster red for 6 minutes
Correlated with search_filter_chips rollout (terms aggregations on brand.keyword)
Flag search_filter_chips disabled and fielddata cache cleared

root_cause: The filter chips feature (flag search_filter_chips, search-api v7.2.0) ran terms aggregations on brand.keyword and attributes.* for every query, loading large fielddata into heap and tripping the parent circuit breaker.
contributing_factors: Feature launched at 50% traffic without load test
No heap alert

remediations.action: Rolling restart of OpenSearch data nodes
remediations.result: Triggered a shard relocation storm; cluster went red for 6 minutes.

remediations.action: Disabled the search_filter_chips flag and cleared the fielddata cache
remediations.result: Heap dropped from 96% to 61%; latency normal in 8 minutes.

action_items.item: Re-implement filter chips with pre-computed facets
Load test gate for features adding aggregations

title: UPI failures again: NovaPay degradation, circuit breaker too slow to trip
impact: UPI success rate 74% for 8 minutes; 312 customers received duplicate UPI collect requests.
symptoms: Circuit breaker still CLOSED after 6 minutes
logs:
2026-07-12T20:31:12.004+05:30 level=warn msg="psp call timeout" psp=novapay op=collect_request latency_ms=10001
2026-07-12T20:34:40.771+05:30 level=info msg="breaker state" psp=novapay state=CLOSED failure_ratio=0.41 window=5m threshold=0.50

timeline.event: Manual payment-retry job triggered for failed transactions
upi_psp_routing flipped to upixpress:100; retry job stopped

root_cause: NovaPay degraded again. The circuit breaker added after INC-2150 used a 50% failure threshold over a 5-minute window, which was too slow to trip at a 41% failure ratio.
contributing_factors: Breaker threshold too conservative
Payment-retry job run while the PSP was still degraded

remediations.action: Ran the manual payment-retry job while NovaPay was degraded
remediations.result: 312 customers received duplicate UPI collect requests.

remediations.action: Flipped upi_psp_routing to upixpress:100
remediations.result: Success rate recovered to 95% within 2 minutes.

action_items.item: Lower breaker threshold to 25% failures over 60 seconds (payments-gateway v4.5)
Block payment-retry job while any PSP breaker is open

title: Kafka lag on inventory.updates again: poison record crashes consumers after WMS firmware update
impact: Stale stock for about 26 minutes in Hyderabad; 2% cancellations.
logs:
2026-08-02T07:47:31.880+05:30 inventory-sync-consumer-2 FATAL Fatal Python error: Segmentation fault (in google.protobuf.pyext decoding topic=inventory.updates partition=5 offset=90117734)
2026-08-02T07:47:32.004+05:30 kubelet Back-off restarting failed container consumer in pod inventory-sync-consumer-2

timeline.event: Consumer pods restarted, crash loop continues
Arjun recognises the INC-2178 pattern; poison record from HYD-KONDAPUR-02 after WMS firmware 5.2

root_cause: WMS firmware 5.2 at warehouse HYD-KONDAPUR-02 changed bundled-item encoding. The record crashed the protobuf C decoder with a segfault instead of raising a validation error, so the automatic DLQ added after INC-2178 never ran.
contributing_factors: Decoder crash bypassed retry/DLQ logic
Vendor firmware updates are not announced

remediations.action: Restarted the inventory-sync consumer pods
remediations.result: Crash loop continued because the consumers re-read the same poison record.

remediations.action: Moved the poison offset to the DLQ with kafka-dlq-skip
remediations.result: Consumers stabilised and lag drained in 13 minutes.

action_items.item: Decode in a subprocess guard so crashes route to DLQ
Pin WMS firmware per warehouse; vendor must announce updates

title: orders-db CPU 98% at midnight: 11 CronJobs fire at 00:00 IST
detected_by: RDS CPU > 90% alert and checkout-api latency alert
impact: checkout-api p99 4s for 18 minutes during the midnight flash sale; about 900 failed orders, plus 2 minutes of full outage during an RDS failover.
logs:
2026-08-10T00:01:12+05:30 rds orders-db CPUUtilization=98.4 DatabaseConnections=412
2026-08-10T00:01:15.330+05:30 checkout-api WARN SlowQuery 3812ms: UPDATE coupons SET status='EXPIRED' WHERE expires_at < now() (coupon-expiry job lock wait)

timeline.event: RDS CPU and checkout latency alerts
Instance class change db.r6g.2xlarge -> db.r6g.4xlarge applied immediately
Multi-AZ failover: orders-db unavailable for about 2 minutes, all writes failed
Identified 11 CronJobs (coupon-expiry, loyalty rollup, GST invoice batch, reports) all at 00:00 after the timezone clean-up
Suspended non-critical jobs and moved GST invoice batch to the read replica

root_cause: The CronJob timezone clean-up (CHG-0809) normalised 11 jobs to '0 0 * * *' Asia/Kolkata, creating a thundering herd on orders-db at midnight, which coincides with the daily flash sale.
contributing_factors: No review of combined schedule
GST invoice batch ran on the primary

remediations.action: Changed orders-db instance class to db.r6g.4xlarge mid-incident
remediations.result: Triggered a Multi-AZ failover with about 2 minutes of full database downtime.

remediations.action: Suspended non-critical CronJobs, moved the GST invoice batch to the read replica and staggered schedules
remediations.result: CPU dropped to 55% within 6 minutes.

action_items.item: Stagger CronJobs (00:00, 00:20, 00:40, 01:30, 02:10) and lint for schedule collisions
Run reporting jobs on the read replica

contributing_factors: INC-2104 action item still open
New on-call engineer unaware of INC-2104
Manual reconcile allowed during peak hours

remediations.action: Rolling restart of checkout-api
remediations.result: Same as INC-2104: errors dropped for about 5 minutes, then returned because the locks were still held.

remediations.result: Pool recovered within 3 minutes.

title: DNS i/o timeouts after EKS 1.32 upgrade: node-local-dns missing on new node group
impact: Pods scheduled on the new node group could not resolve DNS for 45 minutes; 3-7% 5xx across services.
symptoms: Only pods on ng-general-v4 nodes affected
logs:
2026-08-28T16:39:57.201+05:30 search-api: java.net.UnknownHostException: search-os.internal.basketbolt.in: Temporary failure in name resolution
2026-08-28T16:40:03.118+05:30 checkout-api: dial tcp: lookup orders-db.internal.basketbolt.in on 169.254.20.10:53: read udp 10.4.40.7:38812->169.254.20.10:53: i/o timeout

timeline.event: Scaled CoreDNS 6 -> 10 (the INC-2160 fix), no effect
Noticed errors only on ng-general-v4 nodes; node-local-dns DaemonSet had 0 pods there

root_cause: The node-local-dns DaemonSet had nodeSelector nodegroup=ng-general-v3. After the EKS upgrade moved workloads to ng-general-v4 it was not scheduled there, while kubelet still pointed pods at the node-local address 169.254.20.10, so DNS queries on new nodes went nowhere.
contributing_factors: DaemonSet pinned to a node group label
Upgrade checklist did not verify DaemonSets

remediations.action: Scaled CoreDNS from 6 to 10 replicas (the INC-2160 fix)
remediations.result: No effect: pods on new nodes were sending DNS to 169.254.20.10 where nothing was listening; CoreDNS capacity was not the problem.

remediations.action: Fixed the node-local-dns DaemonSet nodeSelector so it runs on the new node group
remediations.result: node-local-dns pods scheduled on all ng-general-v4 nodes; DNS recovered in 4 minutes.

action_items.item: Upgrade checklist: verify all DaemonSets have desired == ready on new node groups

title: Checkout p99 latency 6.1s after config change: HikariCP maximumPoolSize 40 -> 20
impact: Checkout p99 6.1s and 1.2% 5xx for 31 minutes during lunch.
logs: 2026-09-03T12:09:48.610+05:30 WARN  [http-nio-8080-exec-33] c.z.h.p.HikariPool : HikariPool-1 - Connection is not available, request timed out after 30000ms (total=20, active=20, idle=0, waiting=95)

timeline.event: Suspended inventory-reconcile (pattern from INC-2104/INC-2291), no effect
pg_stat_activity shows 0 idle-in-transaction sessions; noticed total=20 in Hikari logs

root_cause: checkout-api v5.12.0 moved datasource settings into the shared library bb-spring-starter 2.3, which defaulted HikariCP maximumPoolSize to 20 instead of checkout's 40. Lunch traffic saturated the smaller pool.
contributing_factors: Shared library default silently overrode service config

remediations.action: Suspended the inventory-reconcile CronJob (INC-2104 playbook)
remediations.result: No effect: reconcile was not running and pg_stat_activity showed no idle-in-transaction sessions. Always check pg_stat_activity before applying the INC-2104 fix.

remediations.action: Rolled back checkout-api to v5.11.4 with Argo CD
remediations.result: Pool back to 40 connections; latency normal in 4 minutes.

action_items.item: Set spring.datasource.hikari.maximum-pool-size=40 explicitly in checkout-api
Alert when HikariCP total connections changes after a deploy

title: Payment webhooks rejected: HMAC signature mismatch after secret rotation
impact: 2,140 paid orders stuck in PAYMENT_PENDING for up to 50 minutes; customers charged but orders not confirmed.
logs: 2026-09-19T10:04:58.337+05:30 level=error msg="webhook signature verification failed" psp=upixpress kid=whsec_2026_09 expected_kid=whsec_2026_06 path=/webhooks/upixpress

timeline.event: Found kid mismatch: pods still using the June secret
Rolling restart of payments-gateway to load the new secret
Replayed webhooks for 10:00-10:41 from the UPIxpress dashboard

root_cause: The quarterly rotation (CHG-0918) updated the UPIxpress webhook secret in the PSP dashboard and in Vault, but payments-gateway only reads secrets at startup, so running pods kept verifying with the old key.

remediations.result: New pods loaded whsec_2026_09 and webhook verification succeeded. Here a restart was the correct fix because the secret is only read at startup.

remediations.action: Replayed missed webhooks from the UPIxpress dashboard for the incident window
remediations.result: All 2,140 pending orders confirmed.

action_items.item: Hot-reload secrets from Vault agent in payments-gateway
Add rollout restart and replay steps to the rotation runbook
